text:
maria: quick async standup — kernel batching fairness + KV eviction perf smoke. did a handful of microburst runs on canary, saw p95 jump during slot steal. details below, tl;dr: possible preemption/starvation when small high-priority requests interleave with large batched seqs.

alex: saw something similar yesterday on eu-canary, logging showed queue lengths spike then a short window of 500–900ms p95. not full OOM, just queuing. :thinking_face:

sam: thanks for the heads up. which commit on the batcher? i reviewed the batching priority change but not the kernel preempt bits yet. pinged you on PR #482.

maria: PR #482 is the batcher fairness patch (reorder by priority + age). i ran with kernel rev 0c9f4b7 (the prefetch/prefill change). repro steps i did:

```bash
# quick perf script
python infra/tools/perf_smoke.py \\  --env=canary \\  --model=redwood-v2-small \\  --seq=1024 \\  --workload=mixed_microburst \
```

logs (snip):
```
[12:31:02] slot=12 accept small req id=0x7f p95=48ms
[12:31:02] slot=12 accept large batch id=0x9a p95=240ms
[12:31:02] preempt check: high-prio queued=3
[12:31:03] slot-steal triggered -> large batch paused -> small reqs run -> large batch resumes -> p95 jump to 640ms
```

devon: interesting — this reads like fairness by priority without a bounded fairness window. high-prio keeps jumping in and pushing the large batch back, walking the large batch's CPU/GPU usage into cache thrash. could be KV warmup churn.

sam: is KV eviction policy LRU? iirc the canary build had a tweak to prefer age over recency for slot eviction. that could make large batches lose cached KV entries more often.

maria: canary was running eviction_policy=age_prefer (experiment flag). i toggled back to lru and re-ran, p95 improved but still higher than baseline. so both batching fairness + eviction interact.

alex: CI got a flaky test in e2e-inference that times out under microburst - ci-bot flagged it: `ci-bot: test/inference/throughput:flaky (timeout)`. @ci-bot any more details?

ci-bot: reproduced timeout on canary-3 with seed=20260317-084, stack snippet attached to PR #482.

maria: next steps i propose:
- short-term: revert eviction experiment on canary and add a bounded fairness window in batcher (e.g., let large batches run for up to 50ms before yielding).
- mid-term: instrument KV eviction telemetry (miss rate vs slot age) and add prefilling heuristics when preemption occurs.
- pairing: i'll pair with devon at 13:00 PT to reproduce on dedicated dev node and collect perf traces.

devon: confirmed, 13:00 PT works. i'll try adding a minimal fairness timer in the batcher and push as a draft.

sam: i'll prioritize the PR review once devon has the draft. also can add a quick perf harness that runs `--mixed_microburst` as part of canary smoke.

alex: small logistic note — we have the infra maintenance window tomorrow 03:00–04:00 UTC; if you need stable canary runs, schedule them now or later.

maria: thanks, all. blocking items:
- need someone to revert eviction flag on canary (volunteer?)
- need perf traces from devon pairing session (we'll attach to PR)

sam: i'll revert the flag now and post the canary link.

alex: :thumbsup: i'll also mute the flaky e2e job for 4h while we iterate.

devon: pairing notes: will try two variants — (A) fairness timer 50ms, (B) prefetch on resume for paused batches. will log kernel events with `TRACE_BATCHER=1`.

maria: if anyone wants to join the pairing, ping me in #eng-runtime; otherwise i'll post the trace + summary after 14:00 PT. :eyes:
